u3745ff808f: Manual programming is slow. Automated programming with a handler greatly increases programming speed and solves the problem of low manual programming efficiency.
ua2847f866d: The handler controls automated programming through IO signals on the programmer, replacing the work of two manual programming steps: ⟦1⟧starting programming⟦/1⟧ (pressing the Start button by hand) and ⟦2⟧determining the programming result⟦/2⟧ (visually checking the red and green lights on the Start button). A robotic arm places the chip in the adapter socket and starts programming; the handler monitors the programming status indicated by the IO signals in real time, then evaluates and handles the programming result.
u3649f7b8a3: IO control signals for automated programming
uf5ea688a14: Connect the handler's automated programming control lines to the "automated programming IO control signal lines" (自动烧录IO控制信号线) of the adapter board; see the "⟦1⟧Adapter board introduction and installation⟦/1⟧" section. The programmer has control signal lines for two channels. Each channel has a ⟦2⟧Start signal line⟦/2⟧, a ⟦3⟧Busy signal line⟦/3⟧, an ⟦4⟧Ok signal line⟦/4⟧, ⟦5⟧V3.3V⟦/5⟧ and ⟦6⟧GND⟦/6⟧. The control signal lines are described in the table below.
ub895874ce2: Low (red light off)⟦1/⟧or high (red light on)
uab461ae6b0: Low (for more than 1mS, then pulled high)
udec1a677fa: ⟦1⟧Start signal line⟦/1⟧: when the input IO pin of the Start button is held low for more than 1mS, the programmer starts programming. A low time of 2mS~20mS is recommended; a somewhat longer low time does no harm. When the Start button is pressed, the ⟦2⟧Start signal⟦/2⟧ is low; when it is released, the signal is high. ⟦3/⟧ ⟦4/⟧
uecbe0bff7f: ⟦1⟧Busy signal line⟦/1⟧: when the Start signal has been pulled low for 1mS or longer, the IO pin of the ⟦2⟧Busy signal line⟦/2⟧ outputs a high level (rising edge) and the programmer starts programming; this corresponds to the green light on the Start button turning on. When programming ends, the IO pin of the ⟦3⟧Busy signal line⟦/3⟧ outputs a low level (falling edge), which corresponds to the green light on the Start button turning off. ⟦4/⟧ ⟦5/⟧
u3962b44382: ⟦1⟧ok signal line⟦/1⟧: on the rising edge of the ⟦2⟧Busy signal line⟦/2⟧, i.e. when programming starts, the ⟦3⟧ok signal line⟦/3⟧ is pulled low (its initial state is either low or high). The falling edge of the ⟦4⟧Busy signal line⟦/4⟧ marks the end of programming: if programming succeeded, the ⟦5⟧ok signal line⟦/5⟧ is pulled low (the red light on the Start button is off); if programming failed, the ⟦6⟧ok signal line⟦/6⟧ is pulled high (the red light on the Start button is on). ⟦7/⟧ ⟦8/⟧
u87040054dd: The ⟦1⟧V3.3V⟦/1⟧ pin of the control signal interface is a 3.3V power supply provided by the programmer; connect it as required by the handler's control module. The ⟦2⟧GND⟦/2⟧ pin of the control interface must be connected to the GND of the handler's control module; ⟦3/⟧ ⟦4/⟧
